problem:
What is the sum of the leading entries of the $1$st, $2$nd, and $3$rd rows in the matrix $A,$ given below?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & -7 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 6 \\ 3 & 0 & 2 & -1 \\ -1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

feedback.problem:
What is the sum of the leading entries of the $3$rd and $4$th rows in the matrix $A,$ given below?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 4 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 6 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
The first non-zero entry of each row (from left to right) is the leading entry. 

Therefore, the leading entries of the $3$rd and $4$th rows of $A$ are $1$ and $6$, respectively.

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 4 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 6 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the answer is $1+6=7.$
